note: Held-out set. Written before any retrieval change it judges; rules and weights are chosen on v1 only. Every organization, document, number and rule here is invented for evaluation. No customer, tenant or personal data. People appear only as roles.

documents.title: Outgoing Loans Procedure
documents.body: A request to borrow an object must reach the registrar nine months before the opening date. The borrower pays for crating, courier travel and nail-to-nail insurance. Objects on paper may be shown for at most four months and then rest for three years. The loan file is closed only when condition report RG-LN-40 is signed at both ends.

documents.title: Gallery Climate Standard
documents.body: Relative humidity in the painting galleries is held between 45 and 55 percent. Temperature is kept between 18 and 22 degrees Celsius. A drift of more than five points in an hour sends a message to the conservator on call. Cases with photographs use silica cassettes that are reconditioned every eight weeks.

documents.title: Insect Monitoring Plan
documents.body: Sticky blunder traps are placed along skirting boards and counted on the first Monday of each month. Three clothes moths in one trap start a treatment. Infested textiles are bagged and frozen at minus 30 degrees for seventy-two hours. Fresh flowers are not allowed in any store.

documents.title: Object Handling Rules
documents.body: Nitrile gloves are worn for metal and lacquer. Clean bare hands are preferred for manuscripts because gloves reduce touch. Nothing is lifted by its handle, rim or arm. Two people move anything heavier than 12 kilograms, and the route is walked empty first.

documents.title: Salvage and Evacuation Plan
documents.body: People leave first and nobody goes back in for an object. When the fire service allows it, the salvage team enters in pairs with a grab list. The grab list names twenty objects for each floor and is kept in the red box by the loading bay. Wet paper is wrapped in polythene and frozen within 48 hours. Wet paintings are kept face up and flat and are never frozen. Wet metal is dried at once with cool air. The salvage wagon carries blotters, head torches, pallets and two pumps, and is checked each April. A quarantine room is set aside so that damp material never returns to a dry store. The insurer is told the same day and photographs are taken before anything is moved unless water is still falling. The plan is rehearsed twice a year, once in daylight and once after closing. A volunteer may carry crates but may not enter until a staff member has signed the entry board. The wagon key code is held at the security desk. The disaster contract number is DRV-6618 and the contractor answers within two hours.

documents.title: Ticket Refunds and Exchanges
documents.body: Tickets for dated exhibitions can be exchanged up to one day before the visit. Refunds are given only when the museum closes. Members book free but a missed booking without notice uses one of six yearly entries.

documents.title: Visitor Photography Rules
documents.body: Visitors may take pictures without flash in the permanent galleries. Tripods and selfie sticks stay in the cloakroom. Filming for sale needs a permit from the press office five working days ahead.

documents.title: School Visits Guide
documents.body: One adult accompanies every eight pupils under eleven. Packed lunches are eaten in the vault room in two sittings. Workshops last 50 minutes and cost 95 crowns for each class. A quiet room is available on request.

documents.title: Travel and Subsistence Rules
documents.body: Staff on a courier trip may claim 52 crowns a day for meals. Hotel nights above 140 crowns need approval from the head of department. Receipts are handed in within 20 days.

documents.title: Holiday Entitlement
documents.body: Permanent staff have 26 days of holiday a year. Holiday is not booked in the two weeks before a major opening. Four days may be kept for the following year.

documents.title: Records Disposal Schedule
documents.body: Accession registers are kept for ever. Closed circuit recordings are wiped after 31 days. Donor letters are kept for twelve years after the last contact.

documents.title: Damage Reporting Procedure
documents.body: Any damage to an object is reported to the head conservator within one hour and the object is left where it is. Fragments are collected in a labelled tray. The form is DM-77 and no repair is tried on the spot.

documents.title: Shop Stock Control
documents.body: The shop is counted on the last Sunday of each quarter. A difference of more than 2 percent is explained in writing. Books that have not sold in eighteen months move to the discount table.

documents.title: Volunteer Induction
documents.body: New volunteers shadow a guide for three shifts. They receive a green lanyard after a safety talk. A volunteer who is absent for ten weeks repeats the safety talk.

documents.title: Light Exposure Limits
documents.body: Watercolours and dyed textiles are lit at no more than 50 lux. Oil paintings may have 200 lux. Ultraviolet filters on windows are tested each spring with meter model UVT-9.

documents.title: Guided Tour Prices (superseded)
documents.body: The former guided tour price was 7 crowns for each adult and 3 crowns for each child. These prices have ended and must not be printed.

documents.title: Acquisition Bid Limits
documents.body: The trust will bid up to 640,000 crowns for the Selwyn astrolabe at the spring auction. The bidder acts through an agent so that the trust is not recognised. The reserve fund covers the buyer's premium.

documents.title: Alarm Coverage Gaps
documents.body: The survey found no motion sensor on the mezzanine stair and a dead contact on the skylight. Night guards walk the mezzanine every 40 minutes until both are fixed.

documents.title: Draft Rota Reform
documents.body: The draft ends split shifts for gallery assistants and adds a floating supervisor. Two weekend posts would become casual. Nobody else has seen these notes.

documents.title: Programme Board Minutes
documents.body: The board moved the clockmakers exhibition to the spring of next year. The catalogue print run was cut to 1,800 copies. A sponsor for the opening night has not been found.

documents.title: Film Night Crew Sheet
documents.body: Five ushers and one projectionist are needed for each film night. Doors open at 18:30 and the courtyard holds 160 chairs. Blankets are returned to the trolley by the gate.

documents.title: Tap Sampling Manual
documents.body: Samples at customer taps are taken after two minutes of flushing, except lead samples, which are taken from the first draw. Bottles for bacteria contain a thiosulphate pellet and are filled to the shoulder. Samples travel in a cool box below 8 degrees and reach the laboratory within six hours. The chain of custody slip is form QW-SMP-18. A sampler never smokes, eats or wears hand cream on a round. Taps with a hose, a filter or a mixer that cannot be removed are passed over and the next house on the list is used. The sampler notes free chlorine, colour and water temperature on the spot. A chlorine reading under 0.2 milligrams per litre is telephoned to the process desk before leaving the street. If a bottle is dropped or the pellet is lost a new bottle is opened and the old one is marked void. Each sampler carries one blank bottle of sterile water that is opened and closed in the van to check for stray contamination. Results for coliform bacteria are ready after eighteen hours. When coliforms are found, three further samples are taken the same day at the tap, upstream and downstream. The public health officer decides whether families are told to boil their water. Records of each round are signed by the sampler and by the desk.

documents.title: Burst Main Response
documents.body: A crew reaches a burst main within 90 minutes in town and three hours in the hills. Valves are closed slowly, over at least five minutes, to avoid a pressure wave. Homes without supply for more than six hours receive bottled water. The job is entered under code BM-RED or BM-AMB.

documents.title: Meter Reading and Estimates
documents.body: Meters are read twice a year. A bill may be estimated once but never two times in a row. A reading that is three times the usual use is checked by a visit before the bill is sent. The handheld reader is model AQ-52.

documents.title: Help With Bills
documents.body: A household in difficulty can spread what it owes over 18 months without interest. Supply to a home is never cut off for debt. A customer on kidney dialysis at home pays a capped bill.

documents.title: Reservoir Dam Inspection
documents.body: The earth dam is walked every week and surveyed each September. Seepage above 4 litres a minute at the toe drain is reported to the dam engineer the same day. Burrows are filled and photographed. Nobody boats within 100 metres of the spillway.

documents.title: Chlorine Store Safety
documents.body: Chlorine drums are stored on their side in a locked bay with a gas detector. The detector sounds at half a part per million and the bay is left on the upwind side. Two trained people change a drum, both wearing breathing sets. An ammonia swab shows a small leak as white smoke.

documents.title: Working in Chambers and Sewers
documents.body: Nobody enters a chamber without a permit and a top man. Air is tested for oxygen, methane and hydrogen sulphide before entry and all the time during work. A permit lasts one shift. The rescue tripod is rigged before the lid is lifted.

documents.title: Drought Action Steps
documents.body: When the upper lake falls below 60 percent in June, garden sprinklers are banned. Below 45 percent, car washes must recycle. Below 30 percent, street standpipes are prepared and tankers are hired.

documents.title: Mineral Dosing Guide
documents.body: Phosphate is dosed at 1.1 milligrams per litre to coat old pipes. Lime is added when the water is below pH 7.2. Dosing pumps are calibrated with a 500 millilitre cylinder every fortnight.

documents.title: Travel and Subsistence Rules
documents.body: Field staff who work past 20:00 may claim 18 crowns for an evening meal. Private cars are paid at 0.4 crowns a kilometre. Claims are made within one calendar month.

documents.title: Holiday Entitlement
documents.body: Permanent staff have 25 days of holiday a year. Standby staff earn one extra day for every four weekends. Holiday is agreed by the depot lead two weeks ahead.

documents.title: Records Disposal Schedule
documents.body: Water quality results are kept for thirty years. Calls to the contact centre are kept for 90 days. Pump logs are kept for five years.

documents.title: Discoloured Water Procedure
documents.body: Three calls about brown water from one street open an event. A crew opens the nearest hydrant until the water runs clear. The contact centre plays a recorded message for that postcode. Laundry damage is paid for up to 75 crowns.

documents.title: Sludge Cake Transport
documents.body: Treated sludge is pressed to 24 percent dry solids and taken to farms by covered trailer. Trailers are washed before leaving the yard. Spreading stops when the soil is frozen. Each load has ticket SLG-3.

documents.title: Pump Station Telemetry
documents.body: A silent pump station is called again after ten minutes and visited within two hours. Batteries at outstations are replaced every four years. Alarm priority P1 wakes the duty controller by telephone.

documents.title: Household Tariff (superseded)
documents.body: The former household tariff was 1.85 crowns for each cubic metre. This tariff was withdrawn and must not be used on any bill.

documents.title: Land Sale Negotiation Note
documents.body: The utility would sell the old filter beds for no less than 2.9 million crowns. The housing developer wants the access road included. The offer lapses on the last day of November.

documents.title: Control Network Weakness Report
documents.body: Two pump stations still accept a factory password and the remote gateway lacks patching. The fix needs a four hour outage at each site.

documents.title: Draft Depot Closure Ideas
documents.body: The draft closes the valley depot and moves its nine vans to the ring road. Night cover would be shared with the gas company. These are the author's own thoughts.

documents.title: Investment Panel Notes
documents.body: The panel put the ozone plant ahead of the new laboratory. The pipe renewal target is 22 kilometres this year. The panel meets next in the third week of February.

documents.title: Examination Room Conduct
documents.body: Candidates are seated ten minutes before the start and nobody is let in after the first half hour. Telephones are switched off and left in a numbered pouch. A candidate who feels ill is walked outside by an invigilator of either desk and the minutes lost are added at the end. Extra time of 25 percent is given when the support office has issued card EX-25. Calculators must be on the approved list and their lids are removed. Water is allowed in a clear bottle without a label. A candidate who finishes early may leave except in the last fifteen minutes. When cheating is suspected the invigilator takes the paper, notes the time, hands over a new answer book and lets the candidate go on. The seating plan and the attendance list are signed by two invigilators and placed in the grey bag. A fire alarm stops the clock, papers are left face down, and the candidates are kept apart on the lawn in silence. The chief invigilator decides whether the sitting goes on. Scripts are counted twice before the bag is sealed with a numbered tag and taken to the strong room. The strong room log is sheet SR-109 and it is checked every evening.

documents.title: Admissions Decisions
documents.body: Applications that arrive by 15 March are read together. Each is scored by two readers and a third reads when the scores differ by more than four points. Offers are sent within six weeks. An applicant may appeal once within ten working days.

documents.title: Welding Workshop Safety
documents.body: Students weld only behind a curtain and with a shade eleven visor. Gas bottles are chained and their valves are closed at the end of the lesson. A fire watch stays for 45 minutes after the last arc. Synthetic clothing is not allowed.

documents.title: Attendance and Follow-up
documents.body: A student who misses three lessons in a week is telephoned by the tutor. Attendance under 85 percent leads to a meeting with a parent or carer. A medical note covers up to five days.

documents.title: Student Bursary Rules
documents.body: Students from homes with an income under 24,000 crowns may have a bursary of 30 crowns a week. The money is paid on Fridays if attendance was full. Tools lists for trades courses are paid for up to 260 crowns.

documents.title: Laptop Loan Scheme
documents.body: A laptop may be borrowed for one term with a deposit of 40 crowns. A cracked screen costs the borrower 60 crowns. Laptops are wiped on return and the loan label is type LT-Blue.

documents.title: Safeguarding Referral Steps
documents.body: Staff who hear a worrying disclosure write down the student's own words and do not promise to keep it secret. The safeguarding lead is told before the end of the day. Nobody investigates alone.

documents.title: Field Trip Approval
documents.body: Trips are put forward four weeks ahead with a risk sheet. One adult goes with every twelve students. A first aid bag and a list of allergies travel on the coach. Overnight trips are signed by the principal.

documents.title: Training Kitchen Hygiene
documents.body: Cooked rice is chilled within 90 minutes and thrown away after one day. Red boards are for raw meat. Probe thermometers are wiped between dishes and tested in ice water each Monday.

documents.title: Library Borrowing
documents.body: Students borrow six books for three weeks. A book that nobody has reserved is renewed by itself. A lost book costs its price plus 5 crowns. Reference volumes carry the shelf mark TH-REF.

documents.title: Coursework Marking
documents.body: Coursework is returned with comments within fifteen working days. Work handed in late loses ten marks for each day up to three days. One piece in ten is marked again by a colleague.

documents.title: Travel and Subsistence Rules
documents.body: Teaching staff at a conference may claim 44 crowns a day for meals. Train tickets are bought by the office. Claims after 60 days are refused.

documents.title: Holiday Entitlement
documents.body: Office staff have 30 days of holiday a year. Teaching staff take holiday only outside term. Unused holiday is lost at the end of August.

documents.title: Records Disposal Schedule
documents.body: Examination scripts are kept for one year. Student files are kept for seven years after leaving. Door entry logs are kept for 60 days.

documents.title: Accident Book Procedure
documents.body: Every injury is written in the accident book before the person goes home. An injury that needs hospital is reported to the safety adviser at once. The room is kept as it was until a photograph is taken.

documents.title: Car Park Permits
documents.body: Permits cost 12 crowns a term and are given first to people who live more than ten kilometres away. Motorbikes use bay M without a permit. Cars in the ambulance bay are towed.

documents.title: Catering Uniform List (superseded)
documents.body: The former catering uniform list asked for two white jackets and one striped apron. The list has been withdrawn and must not be posted to families.

documents.title: Staffing Reduction Proposal
documents.body: The proposal removes eleven posts in construction and saves 520,000 crowns a year. Unions will be told on the second of May. The governors asked for a smaller option.

documents.title: Disciplinary Case Summary
documents.body: A lecturer is suspended over altered coursework grades. The hearing panel recommends a final warning. The examining body has been asked to check 60 scripts.

documents.title: Draft Four Day Timetable
documents.body: The draft teaches on four days and keeps Wednesday for work placements. Lessons would grow to 100 minutes. It has not been discussed with anybody.

documents.title: Heads of Department Briefing
documents.body: Heads agreed to hold the open evening on a Thursday. The plumbing course is full and has 37 names waiting. Printing is limited to 4,000 pages for each department.
